title: Kernel computations for variable deletion and constant coefficients
statement: For a commutative ring A and i≤d, the kernels of MvPowerSeries.killCompl deleting variables below i and of constantCoeff are the ideals generated by the corresponding variables.

source.place: Remark Tag 032C; coefficientwise decomposition by least positive killed exponent

proof.text: Prove the private finite-set coefficient lemma by induction on a finite set S of variables. For S empty all coefficients vanish, so the series is zero. For S with j inserted, let f₀ retain exactly the coefficients whose j exponent is zero. Its coefficients vanish when every S exponent is zero, so induction puts f₀ in the ideal generated by S. Mathlib MvPowerSeries.X_dvd_iff shows X j divides f - f₀. Ideal.span_mono, multiplication closure and addition closure put f in the ideal generated by S with j inserted.

For deletion, take S to be Fin d filtered by j.val < i. An exponent vanishing on S is in the range of Finsupp.embDomain of the remaining-variable embedding, by Finsupp.mem_range_embDomain_iff. Therefore its coefficient in a kernel element vanishes by coeff_killCompl. Apply the finite-set lemma for the reverse inclusion. For the forward inclusion apply Ideal.span_le and killCompl_X_eq_zero to each killed variable.

For constant coefficients, apply the finite-set lemma to all variables. An exponent vanishing on every variable equals zero by Finsupp extensionality, and its coefficient is the constant coefficient. This proves the reverse kernel inclusion. Ideal.span_le and constantCoeff_X give the forward inclusion. The induction includes the empty variable set and uses no nontriviality assumption on A.

proof_origin.place: Remark Tag 032C; coefficientwise argument formalized by A3 using finite-set induction and Mathlib first isomorphism theorem

lean.statement: theorem quotient_first_variables_kernels (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (d i : ℕ) (_hi : i ≤ d) : RingHom.ker (killCompl (R := A) (Function.Embedding.subtype (fun j : Fin d ↦ i ≤ j.val))).toRingHom = Ideal.span {x : MvPowerSeries (Fin d) A | ∃ j : Fin d, j.val < i ∧ x = X j} ∧ RingHom.ker (constantCoeff : MvPowerSeries (Fin d) A →+* A) = Ideal.span (Set.range (X : Fin d → MvPowerSeries (Fin d) A))
